cohort: 93,690 non-anomalous singletons born at 34-41 gestational weeks
finding: In non-SGA newborns, a low chest/head circumference ratio was associated with increased occurrence of adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, while a high ratio was associated with a decreased occurrence.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was more common in non-SGA newborns with a low chest/head circumference ratio and less common in those with a high ratio.
